description:
## Goal

An unchanged request reuses everything and performs essentially no compiler work. An unrelated edit invalidates nothing for the requested root. A relevant edit recomputes only the exact transitive dependents of what changed.

## Priorities

1. Correct semantics by construction: one denotation, one identity, exact ownership, typed comparisons, and no display strings or incidental order as authority.
2. Collapse duplicate concepts and authorities: one World fact authority and one retained ProductMemo authority.
3. Work is edge-triggered by precise source, fact, product, demand, or dependency movement.
4. Equal reproduction preserves allocation and generation, wakes nobody, and deep-copies nothing.
5. Recursive publications converge and retract through the ordinary scheduler.
6. Native compilation is body-incremental.
7. Source replacement owns and withdraws exact contributions.
8. Deterministic causal counts prove less work; wall time and CI duration corroborate.
9. No probes, adapters, duplicate tests, migration scaffolding, or obsolete documentation remain after cutover.

## Architectural decisions

- InputDemand is derived directly from source-owned LoweredBody, EntryDispatch, and exact peer facts. InputFlow, a second semantic body, reconstructed frames, and private demand cones/solvers do not exist in the final model.
- Source identity, validated publication, completed attempts, and consumer-owned semantic support are separate live cutovers. Each replaces a current production path before live replacement exists. Observed reads remain invalidation dependencies; the scheduler routes precise changes but does not infer support from key reachability, finality, source-body reads, or ProductMemo membership. The existing World domain stores remain the sole value authorities.
- submit_source creates a new typed owner. replace_source(owner, text) is the only edit operation. Identical replacement is a no-op. A rejected replacement leaves the accepted version current; failure after acceptance withdraws stale derived claims while retaining exact observations and diagnostics.
- ActivationInputs is the sole correlated input-evidence authority. No activation key is decoded to manufacture evidence.
- Native bodies are exact retained products keyed by semantic codegen inputs. The post-lowering whole-root sharing pass disappears.
- Immutable source versions may remain for exact provenance owners. No duplicate World, rollback image, duplicate semantic state, generic support-value store, or reconciliation pass is permitted.
- Warnings are typed semantic evidence contributed by demanded producer attempts through the ordinary World fact ledger. Warning identity contains no diagnostic text, span, rendered type, or incidental order. The current diagnostic snapshot is an ordinary retained ProductMemo product over exact fact/request/provenance dependencies; it is not a queue, side effect, scan, second cache, or source of semantic demand. Equal reproduction preserves its allocation and generation.

## Accepted DAG

fz-tfn.59 is the sole stack/inclusion frontier. It rebuilds the branch above accepted PR #121 and #122, excludes invalid PR #123, deletes dormant per-derivation scheduler identity as the first real commit, and creates/submits the new draft recalculator PR in the gh stack.

After that boundary:

- fz-tfn.61 gives initial submissions stable typed source owners and immutable provenance versions.
- fz-kdt.27 gives every source struct pattern one typed discriminator and success-owned named-field subjects.
- fz-tfn.64 makes each successful inline dispatch one explicit value-producing control edge, with one exact subject graph, preserved value origins, and construction-owned physical retention; it deletes inline rebinding and the cons side channel atomically.
- fz-tfn.62 preserves callable identity through quoted source and deletes canonical-name re-resolution.
- fz-tfn.53 replaces mutation-before-validation with one typed publication batch per actual producer event.
- fz-tfn.46 completes every job attempt into the existing dependency ledger.
- fz-kdt.82 preserves changed-withdrawal direction as a typed ground shift.
- fz-kdt.64 establishes bounded consumer-owned support for real ReturnType and ActivationInputs alternatives. It absorbs the valid recursive law from fz-kdt.213; there is no scheduler-metadata-only support layer.
- fz-tfn.57 then exposes atomic live source replacement over those proven boundaries.
- fz-kdt.46 makes fact demand and subscription replacement exact-edge-triggered.
- fz-tfn.6 deletes the activation frontier in favor of exact appearance edges.
- fz-tfn.15 removes scan-era scheduling/telemetry/accounting residue.
- fz-tfn.47 gives product requests one exact lifecycle and trigger.
- fz-kdt.188 removes fabricated Cartesian activation evidence.
- fz-kdt.200 derives final InputDemand and activation identity directly from authoritative bodies.
- fz-kdt.48 establishes denotational Ty and exact paired-evidence identity.
- fz-tfn.14 makes ActivationInputs one change-aware store.
- fz-tfn.40 separates executable content from diagnostic provenance.
- fz-kdt.36.1 atomically establishes typed warning evidence in the ordinary World fact ledger, one retained diagnostic-snapshot product in ProductMemo, and function-head coverage derived in the demanded activation attempt after fz-kdt.200 has established final demand/activation identity.
- fz-kdt.36.2 cuts case/with-else coverage onto the same typed warning facts; fz-kdt.36.3 migrates resolver warnings and deletes the warning queue.
- fz-5xp.88 waits for fz-kdt.48's denotational `Ty`/paired-evidence identity and renders canonical reachable failure witnesses; fz-kdt.36.4 proves exact warning reuse/retraction and removes every alternate authority.
- fz-tfn.13 makes native lowering/codegen/linking body-incremental.
- fz-tfn.20 reclaims source versions with no remaining exact owner after warning provenance participates in lifetime; fz-tfn.63 then accepts immediate quoted-source roots.
- fz-tfn.52 and fz-tfn.56 remove residual final-model scheduler/product work.
- fz-kdt.114 audits only residual blocked-wait display ordering and scan residue after the exact-edge cutover.
- fz-tfn.65 makes repeated pattern variables one binding plus one typed equality constraint after both the inline authority cutover and contextual lexical identity.
- fz-tfn.66 makes an already-queued matching message win before `receive after 0` on native doors; it is independent of the pattern cutover and blocks only the final proof.
- fz-tfn.60 is the final exact-reuse and debris-removal proof.

bw dependencies are authoritative for execution order and reject cycles. This prose must be updated whenever the DAG changes; every edge must be necessary and sufficient.

## Ticket consolidation

The following acceptance contracts are absorbed, not discarded:

- fz-tfn.59 absorbs fz-tfn.21 because stack creation needs the first real deletion commit to form one reviewable atomic boundary.
- fz-tfn.53 absorbs fz-kdt.79's exact typed-store/fact lifetime law.
- fz-tfn.46 is restored as the completed-attempt cut; its former absorption into fz-tfn.57 was too broad.
- fz-kdt.64 absorbs fz-kdt.76's reachability/availability distinction, fz-kdt.190's per-correlated-row return refinement, fz-kdt.64's own current grow-only termination witness, and the valid recursive-retraction law from fz-kdt.213. The former scheduler-metadata-only implementation premise of fz-kdt.213 is refuted.
- fz-tfn.57 retains the final replacement contracts from fz-kdt.24, fz-kdt.30, fz-kdt.32, and fz-tfn.45.
- fz-kdt.200 absorbs the valid laws from invalid fz-kdt.214, superseded fz-kdt.220 and fz-kdt.75, the InputDemand-specific obligations formerly associated with fz-kdt.213, and fz-kdt.165.
- fz-kdt.48 absorbs fz-0za and fz-kdt.173.
- fz-tfn.14 absorbs fz-tfn.19.
- fz-kdt.46 absorbs fz-kdt.7.
- fz-tfn.15 absorbs fz-tfn.16.
- fz-tfn.47 absorbs fz-tfn.32.
- fz-kdt.36 is the warning-fact epic. Its former policy fork is resolved: ActivationInputs is the sole function-head coverage domain, contracts affect coverage only through ordinary reached-call application, producer support uses the existing World fact ledger, and retained delivery uses ProductMemo. fz-5xp.88 is reparented and corrected from its obsolete undeclared-any premise. fz-kdt.37 is a downstream consumer of the completed model.
- fz-tfn.13 absorbs fz-tfn.42 and fz-tfn.43.
- fz-kdt.68 is refuted by its measured regression and lack of a production consumer; fz-tfn.59 removes the dormant substrate.
- fz-kdt.13.2 is invalid: its parked per-answer watermarks added 6–10% work with no consumer and depended on the substrate fz-tfn.59 deleted. Its obsolete remote branch is removed.
- fz-kdt.114 remains a narrow post-cutover absence audit. fz-kdt.49 is obsolete as written; global type-mint and row confluence belongs to fz-kdt.48.
- fz-tfn.39 and fz-tfn.54 remain tracked outside this epic. fz-tfn.58 is closed as superseded because fz-5xp.87 already delivered its complete runtime-helper domain scope.
- fz-tt2 owns PR #124's independent dangling-ticket and title correction; it does not block this epic.

## Execution protocol

One implementation ticket equals one code commit and one close. Before creating any new issue, inspect existing tickets and open PRs for overlap, contradiction, and ordering. Correct descriptions directly; do not append contradictory comments.

Hard architectural tickets use a pre-implementation high-capacity validation and a separate fresh cold ticket-scoped adversarial review of the frozen candidate. Reviews assess only the ticket and epic invariants.

fz-tfn.59 created and submitted PR #125 above #122 with gh stacks, and its implementation commit counts as accepted ticket 1. fz-kdt.27 is the next accepted boundary: once its frozen candidate passes cold review, its one commit creates and submits a new draft stack layer above green PR #125 so interim accepted progress is remote and reviewable. Thereafter each stack layer contains at most ten accepted ticket commits; the next completed ticket after each tenth commit creates and submits another draft layer. Work may begin while CI runs, but no later ticket is pushed until the preceding pushed head is green.

## Completion

Same input means reuse; unrelated change means no requested-root work; relevant change means only necessary work, while every semantic answer and required artifact contract remains correct.
